In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $3t(t+2),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit.

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $3$, and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $(t+2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{t+1}{t(t+2)}-\frac{1}{3t} & = \\ \frac{3}{3}\cdot \frac{t+1}{t(t+2)}-\frac{t+2}{t+2}\cdot \frac{1}{3t} & = \\ \frac{3(t+1)}{3t(t+2)}-\frac{t+2}{3t(t+2)} & = \\ \frac{3(t+1)-(t+2)}{3t(t+2)} & = \\ \frac{3t+3-t-2}{3t(t+2)} & = \\ \frac{2t+1}{3t(t+2)} & \end{aligned}
$$
